levels.h2: A workspace for every role, one way of working
levels.lead: K-12 teachers, lecturers and the Quality Assurance Office share one app. K-12 has the full set of writing tools; Courses and Programs have projects, documents and the assistant today, and the rest is on the roadmap.

assistant.h2: Ask, request edits and hand over tasks right on the screen you are working on
assistant.lead: The assistant understands the project and artifact you have open, answers in three tiers of conclusions and offers action cards, so the app does the work when you click.

p1.title: Knows what you are looking at
p1.desc: The “Viewing” chips show each item that is sent. The assistant only receives a structured summary, never the original files; remove a chip and that item is not sent.

p2.title: Local actions cost nothing, AI tasks quote first
p2.desc: Action cards like opening a screen, creating a project or switching AI off run directly on your computer. AI tasks always show a cost range before they run.

p3.title: Clear suggestions, you decide
p3.desc: The assistant's suggestions carry the label “Suggestion, needs human review”. They are text to read; to change something, you edit it on the writing screen, and an approved version stays as it is.

p4.title: Never approves or signs on your behalf
p4.desc: The Approve button lives in the Export step of the main screen. Ask the assistant to approve or sign and it tells you which screen to do it on.

assistant.windowTitle: EduFlow · Results and quality gates (design preview)

pipeline.h2: Five steps, with a person deciding at the last one
pipeline.caption: Each project keeps its steps on your computer so you can reopen it and carry on.

s1.title: Set up
s1.desc: Choose the subject, grade, topic and curriculum framework. You can start with a single sentence to the assistant.

s2.title: AI fills in structured content
s2.desc: The app builds a fixed structure; AI only fills in the content within it.

s3.title: Quality gates check
s3.desc: Each gate prints how many units it checked. A gate that checked 0 units counts as an error and never reports a pass.

s4.title: You review
s4.desc: AI content carries the Suggestion label until you approve it. At K-12, Approve is the last step; editing afterwards creates a new draft.

s5.title: Export files
s5.desc: Tests and lesson plans export to DOCX or PDF, slides to PDF or PPTX; exporting runs on your computer and costs nothing.

t1.title: Your data stays on your computer
t1.desc: Projects, artifacts and chat history stay on your computer. The server only relays content to the model and records token counts; it never stores content.

t2.title: Three tiers of conclusions, never mixed
t2.desc: The deterministic tier states facts with their basis. The comparative tier says “not found yet”. The suggestion tier always needs human review.

t3.title: Zero units checked is not a clean result
t3.desc: The gates that run print how many units they checked; a gate that checked nothing counts as an error.

t4.title: An approved version stays as it is
t4.desc: After approval, editing a test or lesson plan creates a new draft; the approved version is never edited directly.

t5.title: Works offline
t5.desc: Setting up, editing and exporting files keep working offline. Only the AI parts need a connection.

t6.title: Transparent costs
t6.desc: Every AI task shows an estimated cost before it runs and the actual cost after it runs.

cost.h2: Pay for the AI you use; what runs on your computer is free
cost.body: EduFlow charges by the AI tokens used. Quality gates, exporting test versions, compiling and reading documents run on your computer at no cost. Each key has a monthly budget and warns you at 80% usage.

q1.q: What is a license key and where do I get one?
q1.a: A key is issued by your school or Agentra and starts with EDU-. If you do not have one, send a trial request right in the app, or contact Agentra to get a key.

q2.a: Download and open EduFlow, choose Request a trial on the first screen and fill in the form. A trial key works on 1 computer, with a trial budget and an expiry date; each computer can receive only one trial key.

q3.q: Do I need an Internet connection?
q3.a: Yes, to activate, to run AI tasks and to ask the assistant. Setting up, editing and exporting files keep working offline.

q4.q: Where is my data stored, and what does the assistant send?
q4.a: Projects and artifacts stay on your computer. The assistant only sends a structured summary of the open screen; when you ask about documents, only the passages in the chips you keep go with the question. The server does not store content.

q5.a: By the AI tokens used, with a monthly budget per key. What runs on your computer is free. Details are on the Pricing page; schools can contact Agentra for a quote.

q6.q: How many computers can one key be used on?
q6.a: As many as the maximum number of devices on the key. When all slots are used, ask an administrator to revoke an old device through Agentra, then activate on the new computer.

q7.q: Can a school turn off AI for a project?
q7.a: Yes. Switch AI off in the project details and the app sends no AI calls for that project, including the assistant; everything that runs on your computer keeps working as usual.

q8.q: How do I update to a new version?
q8.a: The current version does not update itself in the app. When you need a newer one, go to the Download page, get the latest installer and install it as you did the first time; your projects live in the app's own data folder, apart from the install folder.

q9.a: EduFlow is AI software for teachers and lecturers: matrix-based tests, lesson plans and slides, document loading and an AI assistant, with human review. EduFlow is a desktop app by Agentra JSC for macOS and Windows. Today the app has the full set of writing tools for K-12; for Courses and Programs it has projects, documents and the assistant, while syllabus writing and curriculum review are on the roadmap.

q10.q: How is EduFlow different from ChatGPT?
q10.a: ChatGPT is a general-purpose chat assistant, good for ideas and quick drafts. EduFlow builds the standard structure of each piece of preparation: blueprint and specification, test versions, 5512 lesson plans, quality gates and your review step, with your data on your computer.

cta.h2: Bring EduFlow to your subject group, department or quality assurance office
cta.sub: Download the app to try it, or contact Agentra for a quote based on the size of your school.

features.h2: Every piece of preparation has a standard structure, AI to fill it, and a person to approve it

tests.title: Blueprint-based tests and test versions
tests.body: Build a topic matrix across four levels, let AI write the items, then export up to 24 test versions shuffled with a fixed key. Quality gates check the test; you review each item.

lessons.title: 5512 lesson plans and slides with quizzes
lessons.body: Pick a lesson from the 2018 general education curriculum and let AI draft the four activities of a lesson plan, or the content of 16:9 slides with quizzes; you edit, approve and export.

assistant.title: An assistant that is always there
assistant.body: Ask on the home screen or right beside the screen you are working on. The assistant knows the open screen, answers in three tiers of conclusions, sets up a test, lesson plan or slides for you, shows the cost of every message, and never approves or signs for anyone.

syllabus.title: Documents and the assistant for lecturers, syllabi on the roadmap
syllabus.body: Today lecturers and quality assurance offices create projects, load documents for the app to read on your computer, and ask the assistant about those documents. CLOs, weekly plans, syllabi and curriculum review are on the roadmap and not in the app yet.

q1.q: What can EduFlow prepare for K-12 teachers?
q1.a: Tests built from a four-level matrix, shuffled into several versions with the test specification, answer key and marking guide; Official Letter 5512 lesson plans; lesson slides with quizzes. The app builds the structure, AI fills in the content, and you review and click Approve.

q2.q: Which question types can a test have?
q2.a: Two forms exist today: multiple choice, and a combined multiple-choice and essay form, where essays are scored and come with a marking guide. True or false, short-answer and essay questions with scored sub-parts are on the EduFlow roadmap.

q3.q: How many versions can one test have?
q3.a: Up to 24 test versions. Questions and options are shuffled with a fixed key, so printing again gives the same versions; the answer key and marking guide are separate files.

q4.q: Can I trust answer keys written by AI?
q4.a: When the matrix has application or advanced application items, a second AI pass solves the test again. Any item whose answer changes becomes a warning, and you confirm each item before approving.

q5.q: Does AI publish a test or lesson plan on its own?
q5.a: No. AI content carries the Suggestion label until you click Approve, quality gates have no skip button, and only people approve. At the K-12 level, Approve is the last step. Exports carry the TRIAL (DÙNG THỬ) watermark while the test is not approved, a blocking violation remains, a trial key is in use, the key type of this computer could not be checked or the item is a sample.

outcomes.h2: What works today, and what is on the roadmap

o1.title: A Course project
o1.desc: Create a project at the Course level to keep a course's documents and conversations together. This project has no drafting screen yet.

o2.title: Add lecture materials and textbooks
o2.desc: Add PDF, Word, PowerPoint or image files, up to 80 MB and 300 pages each; the app reads them on your computer and splits them into passages with a section path and page numbers. Scanned pages and photos are not read into text yet; they wait for OCR.

o4.title: Ask the assistant about your documents

o5.title: Keep private parts private
o5.desc: A do-not-send-to-AI switch locks a section or block; turning AI off for the whole project means no content leaves your computer.

o6.title: Roadmap: CLOs, weekly plan, syllabus
o6.desc: Not in the app yet: CLOs with a Bloom-level gate, a weekly plan, session plans, a 10-section syllabus with sources, and approval through a signed package. No release date.

gates.title: Gates G1..G12: on the roadmap
gates.body: By design, twelve gates, G1..G12, check inputs, CLO fields, Bloom levels, weekly traceability, assessment weights, timing, figures backed by a basis and the approval signature. The app does not have these gates for the Course level yet.
gates.rule: A principle already running at the K-12 level: a gate that checked 0 units shows Gate error, never Pass.

cta.h2: Bring your course materials into EduFlow
cta.sub: Download the app, create a Course project and add your documents; the course drafting tools will follow on the roadmap.

q1.q: What does EduFlow do for lecturers?
q1.a: Today: create a Course project, add lecture materials and textbooks so the app reads them on your computer, search passages and ask the assistant about your documents. On the roadmap, not in the app yet: suggested CLOs, a weekly plan, session plans, assessments and a 10-section syllabus with gates.

q2.a: Not in the app yet; it is on the roadmap. By design, a CLO set must have every field of the standard template, with verbs that match the Bloom level; gate G3 catches level mismatches, and you decide the final wording. For now you check CLOs yourself; the course syllabus page explains how to write them.

q3.q: Are my lecture materials sent anywhere?
q3.a: Reading, splitting and searching run on your computer, and the original files stay there. When you ask the assistant, only the passages in the chips you keep go with the question; a passage marked do-not-send-to-AI is never sent, and a project with AI turned off sends nothing off your computer.

q4.q: What does a course syllabus contain?
q4.a: The syllabus builder is not in the app yet; it is on the roadmap. By design it has ten sections following the standard template, each paragraph with its source, built from approved CLOs, weekly plan and assessments; a section only becomes approved when you mark it as passed. The course syllabus page lists the sections a syllabus usually has.

q5.q: How does the head of department approve?
q5.a: Approval through a signed package is on the roadmap, not available at the Course level yet. By design, you send a signed package, a signed version is locked against edits and the server notarizes its hash without seeing the content. For now, approval follows your faculty and school process.

gates.title: Gates K1..K12: on the roadmap
gates.body: By design, twelve gates, K1..K12, check edge provenance, unknown codes, the review date on every result, all seven checks and the prerequisite criteria before the report is signed. The app does not have these gates for the Program level yet.
gates.rule: A principle already running at the K-12 level: a gate that checked 0 units shows Gate error, never Pass.

cta.h2: Bring your program records into EduFlow
cta.sub: Download the app, create a Program project and add your records; the review tools will follow on the roadmap.

q1.q: What does curriculum review in EduFlow cover?
q1.a: Today: create a Program project, add the degree program records, course syllabi and regulations so the app reads them on your computer, search passages and ask the assistant. On the roadmap, not in the app yet: a digital twin with the provenance of every edge and a three-tier review: deterministic, comparative, suggestion. The planned result is an internal working document, not a self-assessment report.

q2.q: What does reviewing at a review date mean?
q2.a: Not in the app yet; it is on the roadmap. By design, every result is tied to a review date. Bases that have expired, bases about to expire and bases not yet in force on that date are three separate figures, never added into one.

q3.q: What do the curriculum map checks cover?
q3.a: Not in the app yet; it is on the roadmap. By design, seven checks: PLO coverage, PI coverage, progression, 5T, overload, gap and duplication. Each check reports how many units it checked, and a check of 0 units is an error, never a pass.

q4.q: How does the criteria overlay work?
q4.a: Not in the app yet; it is on the roadmap. By design, each criterion of Circular 04/2025 has exactly one status: evidence found, evidence expired or not found. Tier 3 suggestions need a person's approval before they enter a report.

q5.q: Can I test a change before making it?
q5.a: Not in the app yet. On the roadmap, a what-if scenario will let you drop a course or change a PLO on a copy of the graph and see how the change spreads to the criteria, on your computer, at no cost.

how.h2: Clear about what the assistant knows and what it may do

c1.title: Knows what you are looking at
c1.desc: The “Viewing” chips list each context item. Only a structured summary is sent; remove a chip and that item is not sent.

c2.title: Answers in three tiers
c2.desc: Tier 1 blocks only quote the app's deterministic results, in the app's own words. Tier 2 says “not found yet”. Tier 3 is a suggestion that needs human review. Every citation opens its source.

c3.title: Action cards
c3.desc: Cards open a screen, create a project, switch AI off for a project or open an editor with the setup filled in: they run on your computer, cost nothing and run only when you click. Generating content with AI still goes through the cost estimate.

c4.title: You make the edits yourself
c4.desc: The assistant's suggestions are text to read; there is no button that applies them to a test or lesson plan. To change something, edit it on the writing screen; editing an approved version always creates a new draft.

never.lead: The assistant only suggests. Asked to do any of these, it tells you which screen to do it on, or that an administrator handles it.
never.n1: Approve a test, lesson plan or slide deck
never.n2: Confirm answer warnings or gate warnings
never.n4: Change the key or account settings

cost.title: Cost per message
cost.body: The message box shows the cost range per message. Every answer shows its actual cost and token count. Clicking Stop still charges for the part already answered.

states.h2: The assistant says why, and local work keeps running
states.lead: Messages are never silently queued; you know right away what you can still do.
states.imageAlt: Design preview, not a screenshot of the app: four states of the assistant panel when offline, with AI off, with the key locked and over budget

s1.title: Offline
s1.desc: The message box is locked; local commands typed with / still run.

s2.title: Project has AI off
s2.desc: Nothing leaves your computer for that project.

s3.title: Key locked
s3.desc: The assistant stops while features that do not use AI keep working; the Check again button asks for the key status again.

s4.title: Over budget
s4.desc: In block mode, the assistant stops until the 1st of next month or until an administrator raises the budget; local work keeps running.

privacy.title: Chat history stays on your computer
privacy.body: Conversations are saved on your computer and can be deleted at any time; the AI assistant card in Settings lets you keep history for 30 days, 90 days or with no limit. The server does not store chat content.

meta.title: EduFlow pricing: billed by the AI tokens you use
meta.description: EduFlow pricing is based on the AI tokens used, with a monthly budget per key and costs shown before anything runs; local work is free. Ask Agentra for a quote.

hero.h1: Pay for the AI you use, and know the cost before it runs
hero.lead: EduFlow is not sold in feature plans. All three levels are open to everyone; costs come from AI calls and are always shown before they run.

s1.title: One key per organization
s1.body: Each school, faculty or individual receives one key for an agreed number of computers.

s2.title: Try it in the app
s2.body: Choose Request a trial on the first screen and send the form. A trial key works on 1 computer, with a trial budget and an expiry date.

s3.title: Measured in tokens
s3.body: Every AI call measures four token classes: input, output, cache write, cache read. Each class has its own unit price per model.

s4.title: Locked in when recorded
s4.body: The amount for each call is locked in when it is recorded, at the current price list; a new price list only applies to later calls.

s5.title: Know before it runs
s5.body: Every AI task shows an estimated range before it runs and the actual cost after it runs. Assistant messages show the cost under each answer.

s6.title: Monthly budget per key
s6.body: An administrator sets the monthly budget and warn or block mode for the key. The app notifies you at 80% and 100% of the budget.

s7.title: Monthly reconciliation
s7.body: Agentra can export your organization's monthly usage as CSV, each call with its tokens and amount, for reconciliation. It is not an invoice.

formula.title: The formula for one AI step
formula.expr: Cost = sum over classes (tokens in the class × class unit price) ÷ 1,000,000
formula.note: Unit prices are in VND per million tokens, by model and token class. This page does not publish unit prices; schools receive a quote from Agentra.

budget.h2: Three states of the monthly budget

near.title: Near the limit
near.desc: From 80% of the budget, the home screen shows a warning, once per threshold per month on each computer. The estimate dialog shows the budget left for the month.

over.title: Over budget
over.desc: Warn mode: tasks keep running. Block mode: AI tasks stop until the 1st of next month or until the budget is raised.

budget.essential: When blocked, local work such as opening projects, editing, running gates and exporting files keeps working, so your exports never get stuck.

meta.title: AI and data transparency for schools
meta.description: AI transparency at EduFlow: where AI is used, what data it sends, which data stays on your computer, what the server logs, and why people make the decisions.

transparency.lead: This page sets out which of the app's skills use AI, what data is sent and which data never leaves your computer.

p1.title: Where AI is used
p1.body: In the current version, AI fills in structured content for test questions, answer verification, the lesson plan body and its review, slide content, slide theme suggestions and the chat assistant. Everything else runs on your computer.

p2.title: Model tiers
p2.body: Each skill runs on the fast, standard or strong tier; Agentra maps each tier to a specific model. In the Export step of a test, lesson plan or slide deck, a note lists the AI steps that ran, the tier, the actual cost and when the version was made.

p3.title: Data sent out
p3.body: Each call sends only the content the skill needs, under a strict data contract. The assistant sends a structured summary of the open screen, the document passages in the Viewing chips and the latest messages of the conversation, never the original files.

p4.title: Data that stays on your computer
p4.body: The project store, chat history and activation secrets stay on your computer. Imported files are read locally and the original files are never sent; scanned pages and photos are not read into text yet.

p5.title: The server stores no content
p5.body: The server relays content to the model and records token counts, amounts and hashes. Content is neither stored nor written to logs.

p6.title: The machine suggests, people decide
p6.body: AI content carries the Suggestion label until you approve it. There is no button to skip a quality gate; the assistant does not approve or sign.

p7.title: Three tiers of conclusions
p7.body: Tier 1 (deterministic) is a sentence the app itself writes for one of its facts, with a Basis line. Tier 2 opens with “Not found yet” for what the assistant has not seen. Tier 3 carries the label “Suggestion, needs human review”.

p8.title: AI off per project
p8.body: Switch AI off in the project details and the app sends no AI calls for that project, including the assistant.

signed.title: Digitally signed installers
signed.body: The macOS build is signed with a Developer ID and notarized by Apple; the Windows build is code-signed by Agentra JSC. Windows SmartScreen may still ask for confirmation on a newly released version; the installation guide explains what to do.

unsigned.title: Your computer asks again the first time
unsigned.body: The installers are not signed yet with Apple and Microsoft certificates, so macOS and Windows SmartScreen block the first launch and ask again. The installation guide shows each step; only use files downloaded from this page.

update.title: Already installed?
update.body: The current version does not update itself in the app. When a new version is out, download the latest installer from this page and install it as you did the first time; your projects live in the app's own data folder, apart from the install folder.
